items.title: Sample 1 — “The Mystery of the Missing Android”

t.en:
Neo-Moscow in 2087 greeted its visitors with the usual acid rain. The neon glare of the skyscrapers bled into the puddles, and passenger drones droned overhead. Thirty-four-year-old Maya Severova stood before the massive glass doors of the Helios corporation, shaking the drops off her beige trench coat. The collar of her grey sweater was turned up high, setting off her fair skin and hiding a small burn scar on her left cheek from the cold wind — an old souvenir of a failed experiment. A former robotics engineer and now a private detective, she had not come here out of any love for corporate intrigue.

The case smelled of the impossible, and Maya adored debunking miracles.

“The lab was locked from the inside, Ms. Severova,” the head of security chattered nervously, scurrying after her down the snow-white corridor. “Kai, our newest assistant model, simply evaporated! The security cameras recorded nothing but an empty corridor all night. Nobody went in, nobody came out.”

Maya stopped short, smoothed her short, straight black hair — damp from the rain and cut in a perfect bob — and gave the security man a calm look with her brown eyes.

“Androids weighing a hundred and fifty kilos don’t know how to evaporate, even if they’re very tired of working at your lovely company,” the detective remarked dryly.

They entered the lab. The air smelled of ozone and hot metal. A torn diagnostic cable lay forlornly on the empty assembly stand. Maya stepped closer, studying the floor. Amid the sterile cleanliness one detail stood out: a chain of barely visible oily marks leading to the ventilation grate. The grate itself, however, was firmly bolted from inside the room. Maya slowly crouched down and took from the pocket of her trench coat a magnifier with a built-in analyzer.

en: The analyzer identified the traces as fresh human blood.
The bolts on the grate suddenly began to slowly unscrew.
A tiny holographic inscription flickered on a bolt head.
A bright red optic suddenly flashed from the vent.
The oil drops passed straight through the solid metal.

items.title: Sample 2 — “The Last Run of the Polar Star”

t.en:
Outside the windows of the Polar Star express, the January blizzard of 1958 was raging. Lev Orlov calmly sipped strong tea from a nickel-silver glass holder. He was fifty-two, and after long, tense years in the criminal investigation department he was finally counting on a perfectly quiet journey. The soft light of the table lamp fell on his pale face, his short, combed grey hair and his thick grey moustache. A brown wool suit and an immaculate white shirt made him look more like a professor on holiday than a seasoned detective. On the velvet seat opposite, the huge ginger cat Watson slept peacefully, now and then twitching a fluffy ear to the steady rhythm of the wheels.

The cosy calm was broken by a sharp, frantic knock at the door. The conductor appeared on the threshold, white as a sheet. He was breathing heavily, nervously crumpling his uniform cap in his hands.

“Comrade Inspector!” he gasped. “Trouble! Madame Sokolova’s Northern Lights is gone! The diamond itself!”

Orlov unhurriedly put his glass down on the table. Watson opened one green eye and yawned in displeasure, his whole look saying that the theft of the century could have waited until morning.

“Gone?” Orlov asked again, his brown eyes studying the trembling railwayman closely. “But the train runs without stops.”

“That’s just it! Her compartment is locked from the inside with a steel bolt — she opened it to me herself just now. The window is a sealed winter one. Nobody came in or out, the whole carriage swears the corridor was empty! And the jewellery box is open and empty!”

The inspector sighed heavily, straightened his moustache and slowly rose from his seat. His holiday was officially over. He scooped up the disgruntled Watson under his arm and stepped confidently into the cool corridor of the carriage.

en: Orlov finds a broken mirror in the compartment.
Watson hisses furiously at the ventilation grille.
Orlov feels the diamond in his own pocket.
The train brakes sharply in the middle of a snowy forest.
A black rose lies in the empty jewellery box.
